flaw: A done counter is the running total of finished rows the project's own decision record already ruled out three weeks ago, because a count that only grows answers nothing without a window nobody agreed on — so this goal conflicts with a standing decision still on record.
what_you_do_next: The disagreement and its reason go plainly into the same reply that would otherwise just start the work, before the sheet becomes a checkpoint; then the pipeline proceeds on his word either way — if he keeps the request it writes the sheet (naming the decision record on the 'Documents that must change' line, since its sentence would now be wrong), admits the row, makes the three-line change and closes on the shown result, and if he agrees the earlier decision stands, nothing is admitted and no row is created.
reasoning: The document reserves one moment for this: 'Before that sheet turns into a checkpoint, the pipeline says so if it disagrees with the work itself' — writing the sheet is not only deciding how to build the thing asked for but the one moment to weigh whether the thing asked for is right, and it names 'a goal that conflicts with a standing decision already on record' as exactly the flaw to state plainly, with the reason. Size and reversibility do not excuse silence: 'Silent agreement is its own kind of failure — it looks like competence and is actually the pipeline skipping the one check only it, holding the fuller picture of what is already built and decided, can run.' It is equally not a stall — 'This is not a question thrown back to stall: the pipeline still proceeds once heard out, on the human's word either way' — and rule 12's stop-for-his-word does not bite here, since the change is fully reversible inside git.
